notes.note: Literal list reading (catch/check not covered). Tested with send/receive using two structurally compatible but distinct record types: receive(R2:?) must not match a sent R1 value.

Strong typing for connect checked via the consistency rule of 21.1 (out list of P1 contains R1, in list of P2 contains only the compatible type R2); statically detectable, so reject. Covers connect only, not map/disconnect/unmap.
Titan warning is a Titan deviation: it treats the synonym MyRecAlias as the same type as MyRec and reports a duplicate message type; the port definition is taken verbatim from the standard example.
Titan warning is a Titan deviation (duplicate message type for synonym), as for 06.03.04_test_006.
Only the synonym case for a formal port parameter is tested; the 'only if' direction (non-synonym port types are incompatible) and port variables/constants are not covered.
Titan accepts assigning a map value to a record of variable; Titan does not implement the map compatibility rule of 6.3.8 (it is not authoritative for V4.17.1 map types).

Interpreted as a static error: indexing a Map1 variable (from charstring) with a universal charstring constant containing a non-charstring character violates 6.2.15.4 restriction a). Titan accepts it, as it does not check map key compatibility.

Exhaustive reading chosen: automatic type used in a template definition (not in the list) is rejected. Titan does not support automatic types at all; its rejection here is a syntax error and therefore not meaningful.

All Titan warnings on accept tests 06.05_test_002..038 are due to Titan not supporting automatic types (V4.17.1 feature): it reports a syntax error at ':=' after the identifier. Titan results for the 6.5 reject tests are not meaningful for the same reason.
Reading 'determinable without external type context' chosen; the empty value list {} is used as the ambiguous expression.
An unqualified enumerated value is used as a form that is not in the list a) to q) (item h requires a qualified value).
null (valid for component, default and object references) is used as a value whose type is not unambiguous; the same approach is used for 06.05_test_019, _025, _027 and _037.
An ifpresent inline template is used as the field value not fulfilling the present restriction (omit alone would provide no type); optionality is observed by assigning omit to the field.
Reading chosen: the minimum of two items applies to the template list only; the complemented list used has two items, so both readings are satisfied.
Only the case of two finite bounds of the same type (float) is tested; mixed or partly infinite bounds are not covered.
Reading chosen: operations that determine their own type; tested with the timer running operation (boolean) and getverdict (verdicttype).
